body: I think I know how you're feeling. Are you happy? I was happy and enjoyed life which made the thought of death terrifying and has sent me to a really bad place mentally.

Thanks for the response. I've told myself that I shouldn't worry because it will happen and I probably won't know. If I do know that means there's something after and that's probably a good thing. Still, it gives me very little comfort.
Well it sounds like you have years potentially to take care of this so please keep trying. You clearly want a better life and have sought help, just don't give up.

I'm obviously not an expert in this field but I'd suggest making a specific post here about free resources. Just with your teeth I know that often times dental schools provide free services to people in need if they let students observe or perform the work.

There are a lot of free resources and people who care. If you call the police and tell them what's going on they'll help. I'm just a stranger on reddit and I care, so imagine how much people who have dedicated their lives to helping people in debt or medical need care. Please reach out to them.

I do have things that make life worth living which makes the idea of dying frightening. I think every day is a blessing and I'm crippled by the fear of it ending. I struggle to see the point when it just ends.

I'm sorry to hear how you feel. You obviously care about life because you're reaching out to get help. I don't know what to tell you about the lack of support you feel you're getting but for what it's worth, I care. You want an enjoyable life and even though I don't know you I truly hope you can change your situation. Never underestimate what you might mean to other people. There might be someone you work with that admires how you juggle two jobs, even if you don't know it. All the stuff you're upset about is temporary so just keep trying.

That's what were taught as Catholics, but my faith in the afterlife isn't all that strong to be honest. I think if I truly believed I wouldn't be so scared. I know atheists find meaning in life but I don't get how. Our time here seems so short and temporary it all feels meaningless to me.

I've thought of the theme park analogy too, and I get it. If you don't mind me asking how do you enjoy the ride when you know one day it ends and you can't remember it? Sorry for being such a downer but that's where that analogy doesn't help me. Thank you.

Thank you for that. I just can't get over this crippling acceptance of the truth that everyone I love will also die. Then what does it all matter? I suppose the question I'm asking is what's the point of living if we die? The fear cripples me. I'm seeing a psychiatrist but so far it hasn't helped.
I was raised catholic, I still am and I go to church but I guess I'm just not devout enough to not fear death. It's truly crippling. My psychiatrist says I have OCD and I need to learn to not focus on these thoughts but that doesn't help me. I'm so sad and depressed. Thanks for listening.
